# A branch that undoes its own change must not have it resurrected by the merge.
# Theirs adds ops and takes it away again (via --group, the absolute set); the
# net effect over their two commits is nothing, so the merged log must not carry
# ops. Our own unrelated group stays.

sesam-repo

# Base: bob in dev.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob'

# OURS: bob gains sec.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add sec
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: bob += sec'

# THEIRS: bob gains ops, then loses it again.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: bob += ops'
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: bob -= ops'

exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs

# ops was added and removed on their side; only our sec survives on top of dev.
exec sesam verify --verify-mode no-disk
exec sesam user ls
stdout 'bob'
stdout 'sec'
! stdout 'ops'
